title: Ston, Croatia with Teenagers: Family Guide 2027
metaDescription: Family travel with teens in Ston, Croatia: wall climbs, kayaking in Mali Ston Bay, oysters, beaches and day trips, with euro prices and opening hours.
content:
## Is Ston a good destination for families with teenagers?

Yes, with one condition: the teens need to be happy with a quiet town. Ston has about 2,500 residents, no nightlife and no water park. What it has is a 5.5 km medieval wall that climbs a steep hill, a sheltered bay for kayaking, working salt pans, and a short drive to beaches and Mljet. It is cheaper and far less crowded than Dubrovnik, which lies about 55 km south. Most families stay two nights, or visit as a long day trip from Dubrovnik.

## Best activities for teens in Ston

### Climb the Walls of Ston

The walls link Ston with Mali Ston over the hill between them. The climb between the two towns is about 1 km one way but steep, with uneven stone steps. Allow 60–90 minutes with breaks. From March to October an adult ticket is €10 and a youth ticket (12–18) is €5. From November to February prices drop to €5 and €2. The same ticket covers the Veliki Kaštio fortress.

Opening hours change by season. April–May and August–September the walls generally open at 8:00 and close around 18:30. June–July they stay open until 19:30. In winter (November–March) hours are roughly 9:00 to 15:00. Start early in summer. The stone has no shade, and midday temperatures often pass 30°C.

The handrails are limited and the steps are polished by foot traffic. Teens need real shoes, not flip-flops.

### Kayak in Mali Ston Bay

The bay is a protected nature reserve with calm water, which makes it suitable for beginners aged about 12 and up. Local operator Ston Adventure runs half-day and sunset tours of about 3 hours, and rents kayaks by the hour, half day or full day. Ston Outdoors also runs guided paddles around the oyster farms. Tours run only when the weather is safe, so book for your first day and keep the second as a backup.

The route passes oyster and mussel farms and small islands, and shows the walls from the water. Paddling along the shoreline is the best way to see how large the wall system is.

### Visit the Ston Saltworks

The saltworks beside Ston are among the oldest in Europe still in use. An individual ticket with a short film on salt harvesting is about €7. Salt is raked by hand in late summer, so August and early September are the best months to see work in progress. The visit takes 30–45 minutes, which suits teens who tire of history quickly.

### Try oysters on the water

Mali Ston Bay is known for European flat oysters and mussels. Several boat tours take small groups to the farms for a tasting, typically five oysters per person. Teens who like food can try them. Others can stick to cooked mussels or grilled fish. Most boat tastings serve wine to adults, and soft drinks are usually available on request.

### Swim at Prapratno and take a day trip to Mljet

Prapratno is a pebble-and-sand beach with pine shade about 5 km from Ston. The Mljet ferry leaves from the same port, and the crossing takes roughly an hour. Mljet National Park has two saltwater lakes where teens can rent bikes and kayaks. Check the current ferry timetable before travelling, and take a car on board only if you plan to stay overnight.

## Where to eat with teens in Ston

The town is small, and restaurants are within a 5-minute walk of the wall gates. Konoba Dardin and Stagnum are both in Ston. Mali Ston has several oyster restaurants along the waterfront. Mussels, grilled fish and pasta are on most menus. Starters of baked or raw oysters usually cost a few euros each. Plan lunch at 12:00 or earlier, because kitchens in town often close between lunch and dinner.

## Sample 2-day plan

| Day | Morning | Afternoon |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Walls of Ston at 8:00 (walk to Mali Ston) | Lunch with oysters or mussels, then kayaking or sunset paddle |
| 2 | Saltworks visit, then Prapratno beach | Mljet day trip or relaxed swim and early dinner in Ston |

## Getting there and getting around

From Dubrovnik, the drive takes about 1 hour by car and a regular bus connects the two. Having a car matters here. It makes Prapratno, the Pelješac vineyards and Mljet far easier. Parking in Ston is limited in July and August, so arrive before 10:00. Within Ston and Mali Ston everything is walkable.

## Honest opinion: skip the Dubrovnik walls for this

Families often spend €35–40 per person on the Dubrovnik city walls and stand in queues. For teens, the Ston walls are the better value. They cost €10 for adults and €5 for ages 12–18. They are longer, steeper and much emptier, and they feel more like a real hike. Do Ston first.

## Local tips

- Buy tickets at gate A or C. The price is the same, and gate A gives access to the full route.
- Bring at least 1 litre of water per person. There are no shops on the wall.
- Visit in May, June or September. July and August are hot and busy.
- Ston has limited phone signal on the hill, so agree a meeting point in advance.
- The Festival of Oysters on St. Joseph's Day (19 March) is a good cultural stop, but fewer activities run in March.

## Where to stay

Stay in Ston or Mali Ston for walkability. Apartments with a kitchen suit families with teens better than hotel rooms, because one room rarely fits everyone. The other option is Prapratno, which has a campsite near the beach. Book at least two months ahead for July and August.

faq.question: How many days do you need in Ston with teenagers?
faq.answer: Two days is enough for the walls, kayaking, saltworks and a beach stop. A single day works as a trip from Dubrovnik, but then you have to choose between kayaking and a long wall walk.

faq.question: How much does it cost to climb the Walls of Ston?
faq.answer: From March to October, adults pay €10 and youths aged 12–18 pay €5. From November to February, prices fall to €5 for adults and €2 for youths. The ticket includes the Veliki Kaštio fortress.

faq.question: Are the Ston walls hard for teenagers?
faq.answer: The walk is steep with uneven stone steps, but most healthy teens manage it in 60–90 minutes. There is almost no shade, so go early and bring water. Closed shoes are strongly advised.

faq.question: Is kayaking in Mali Ston Bay suitable for beginners?
faq.answer: Yes. The bay is sheltered and calm, and local operators run guided tours of about 3 hours. Tours depend on the weather, so keep a spare day in your schedule.

faq.question: Is there a beach near Ston?
faq.answer: Prapratno beach is about 5 km from Ston, with pebbles, some sand and pine shade. It is also the departure port for ferries to Mljet.

faq.question: Is Ston better than Dubrovnik for teens?
faq.answer: For active teens, yes. Ston offers hiking, kayaking and fewer crowds at a lower price. Dubrovnik has more nightlife, shops and film-location attractions, so many families combine the two.

quickAnswer: Ston suits teenagers who like active, hands-on days. The 5.5 km walls cost €10 for adults and €5 for ages 12–18 (March–October). Add a 3-hour kayak tour in Mali Ston Bay, a swim at Prapratno beach and a Mljet ferry day. Two full days are enough.
